In this paper, we present a detailed analysis of the molecular interstellar medium at z = 6.9, through high resolution observations of the $\rm CO(6-5)$, $\rm CO(7-6)$, $\rm CO(10-9)$, \[CI\]$\rm (2-1)$, and p-$\rm H_{2} O (2_{1,1}-2_{0,2})$ lines and dust continuum emission with the Atacama Large Millimeter/submillimeter Array (ALMA).
We use realistic non-Local Thermodynamic Equilibrium (non-LTE) models and estimate the physical properties of the ISM in both the galaxies.
We obtained observations of different emission lines and the continuum using ALMA Band 3 and 4 over three tunings (Project ID: 2017.1.01168.S, PI: Vieira).

In this code, the background source is parameterized by one or more S$\rm \acute{e}$rsic (cite: sersic68) profiles with seven free parameters: source position relative to the lens ($\rm x_{S}, y_{S}$), flux density (S), half light radius major axis ($\rm a_{S}$), S$\rm \acute{e}$rsic index ($\rm n_{S}$), axis ratio ($\rm b_{S}/a_{S}$), and position angle ($\rm \phi_{S}$).

The lensing source is represented by one or more Singular Isothermal Ellipsoids (SIEs), which has five free parameters: the center of the lens relative to phase center ($\rm x_{L}$, $\rm y_{L}$), the lens mass ($\rm M_{L}$) which determines the strength of lensing, the ellipticity of the lens ($\rm e_{L}$), and the position angle of the lens major axis ($\rm \phi_{L}$) in degrees east of north.

This is the most detailed study of molecular gas content of a galaxy in the EoR to-date, with the most distant detection of $\rm H_{2}O$ in a galaxy without any evidence for active galactic nuclei in the literature.
We detect p-$\rm H_{2} O (2_{1,1}-2_{0,2})$ in W with a signal-to-noise $\sim$4 above the continuum.

From the top panel in Figure 11, we see that the magnification is consistent between the CO transitions and the dust continuum, i.e., we do not observe differential magnification between these components in SPT0311-58 W.
From the bottom panel of the figure, we see that the CO emission area is marginally decreasing with increasing excitation level.
Both the galaxies in SPT0311-58 peak at J$_{\rm up}$ $\sim$ 6, similar to other high-redshift starburst galaxies.

The ratio of $\rm T_{kin}/T_{dust}$ is $>$ 1 in both galaxies, which indicates that there are additional heating mechanisms such as X-rays, stellar outflows, and supernovae in addition to photoelectric heating in dense molecular gas.
We fit a linear function to the main sequence galaxies and the SPT-SMGs using MCMC and find a statistically significant correlation between $\rm \alpha_{CO}$ and $\rm T_{dust}$.
We find no evidence of evolution of depletion time with redshift in SMGs at z $>$ 3.
The p-$\rm H_{2} O (2_{1,1}-2_{0,2})$ luminosity in SPT0311-58 W and E is consistent within the scatter of the other high-redshift ULIRGs.

From the $\rm L_{H_{2}O}$-$\rm L_{FIR}$ correlation, we estimate a SFR of $\rm 4356 \pm 2143\ M_{\odot}yr^{-1}$ in W and an upper limit of $\rm 385\ M_{\odot}yr^{-1}$ in E. The SFR calculated from $\rm L_{IR}$ is $\rm 5046 \pm 944\ M_{\odot}yr^{-1}$ in W and $\rm 701 \pm 151\ M_{\odot}yr^{-1}$ in E.

From the top panel in Figure 11, we see that the magnification is consistent between the CO transitions and the dust continuum, i.e., we do not observe differential magnification between these components in SPT0311-58 W.

$\rm T_{kin}/T_{dust} = 2.0 \pm 0.9$ and $3.4 \pm 1.3$ in SPT0311-58 W and E, respectively, which suggests that there are other heating mechanisms in addition to photoelectric heating (traced by $\rm T_{dust}$).
We get a turbulence energy of $\rm \sim 1 \times 10^{59}\ ergs$ in W and $\rm \sim 1 \times 10^{57}\ ergs$ in E, similar to the total CO cooling energy.

The mechanical heating from stellar outflows and supernovae explosions, some of which is converted into turbulent energy, may contribute significantly to the total CO cooling over the depletion timescale.

The CO-to-H2 conversion factor ($\rm \alpha_{CO}$) and the gas depletion time scales estimated from the model are consistent with the high-redshift SMGs in the literature within the uncertainties. We find no evidence of evolution of depletion time with redshift in SMGs at z $>$ 3.

However, this evolution does not seem to exist in the SMG sample at z $>$ 3. In SPT0311-58 W and E, the depletion time obtained from both the methods are within the typical range for high-redshift SMGs.
In this paper, we combine the previous observations with high resolution molecular line imaging with ALMA, including the high-J CO transition, $\rm CO(10-9)$ and p-$\rm H_{2} O (2_{1,1}-2_{0,2})$.
For the continuum flux density in B3, we use the current observations which are at a higher resolution of $\sim$0.5$''$ compared to previous observations at $\sim$3.5$''$.

Since the spectral lines are non-Gaussian and blended in the case of $\rm CO(7-6)$ and \[CI\]$\rm (2-1)$, and $\rm CO(10-9)$ and p-$\rm H_{2} O (3_{1,2}-2_{2,1})$, we use \[CII\] from the ALMA 240 GHz observations (cite: marrone18) as a template to derive the spectral properties.
Since the signal-to-noise is not sufficiently high for pixellated modeling, we use a parametric lens modeling code, `visilens` (cite: spilker16).
The analysis is performed in the visibility plane instead of the image plane to account for the correlated noise in the interferometric images.
Since the signal-to-noise is not sufficiently high for pixellated modeling, we use a parametric lens modeling code, `visilens` (cite: spilker16).
However, due to the increased degeneracies with increased number of free parameters, we use 1 and 2 components in this analysis.
Since $\rm CO(3-2)$ is spatially unresolved ($\sim$5 $-$ 6$''$) into W and E, we distribute the flux density of $\rm CO(3-2)$ by scaling to $\rm CO(6-5)$ in the two galaxies.

Since we do not have a good signal-to-noise for lensing reconstruction in E, we adopt a magnification of 1.3 for all the molecular lines. For the same reason, we adopt $\mu = 2.2$ from (cite: marrone18) in p-$\rm H_{2} O (2_{1,1}-2_{0,2})$ in W.
However, it has to be noted that, due to the lack of \[CI\]$\rm (1-0)$ observations, we cannot reliably confirm the relationship between \[CI\] abundance and gas density.
The non-detection of \[CI\]$\rm (2-1)$ and p-$\rm H_{2} O (2_{1,1}-2_{0,2})$ in E gives large uncertainty on the depletion time estimate.
However, it has to be noted that, while T$_{\rm K}$/T$_{\rm dust}$ is a function of visual extinction (cite: tielens85), we consider a constant value at all extinctions.
One caveat is that we do not consider the change in $\rm T_{kin}$/$\rm T_{dust}$ with density in the LVG model.

However, since we do not have observations of the two important coolants \[OI\] and \[SiII\], which are found to contribute to more than 50% of the total cooling budget (cite: rosenberg15), we cannot provide the complete picture of the neutral gas.
